subject: maths

moments.title: Hamilton's bridge insight
moments.body: Walking by the Royal Canal in Dublin, Hamilton has a sudden insight: a 4D number system with three imaginary units i, j, k. He carves i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = ijk = -1 into Brougham Bridge.
moments.takeaway: The first non-commutative algebra is carved into a Dublin bridge.

moments.title: Vector calculus
moments.who: Josiah Willard Gibbs, Yale; Oliver Heaviside, England
moments.body: Gibbs and Heaviside extract the vector calculus from quaternions. Physics goes with vectors; quaternions are sidelined.
moments.takeaway: Hamilton's framework is replaced by simpler vectors for most physics.

moments.title: Quaternions in computer graphics
moments.body: Quaternions are perfect for representing 3D rotations smoothly without singularities. Every modern 3D game engine, robotics simulator, and spacecraft attitude controller uses quaternions.
moments.takeaway: Hamilton's apparent dead end is now everywhere.

moments.title: Geometric algebra revival
moments.body: Clifford / geometric algebra revives Hamilton's approach in a higher-dimensional setting. Applications in physics, robotics, computer vision.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Vector calculus dominates undergraduate physics. Quaternions dominate 3D graphics and spacecraft. Clifford algebra ties them together.
now.open_questions: Will geometric algebra unify physical formalism?

reflection: Hamilton thought quaternions would supersede vectors. They became niche, then crucial for VR. How do we evaluate which mathematics matters?
